answer: Require each agent identity to keep one unique encrypted data shard in the kernel of its own storage node: auditors issue random retrieval challenges, and an identity that cannot return its shard within seconds loses its weight. One shard backs one identity, and two keys sharing storage are both dropped. Faking 1,000 identities means keeping 1,000 distinct 10 GB shards, about 10 TB at roughly $200 a month, a cost that spreads like a delta into an island of disks no farm can hide.
